green-builder-feb-2012: Which green products deserve a place in your next project? Our Hot 50 picks weigh innovation against reliability and real-world impact. From insulation and windows to lighting and energy systems, this issue looks at practical improvements that work together to make a better home.
green-builder-jan-2016: Good homes can do more with less energy. Our annual awards issue visits standout green projects and explores renewable power, thoughtful design and new housing ideas. A storm-ready Solar Decathlon home shows how efficiency and resilience can work together when a community needs them most.
green-builder-jan-feb-2017: A smart home should do more than answer voice commands. This issue connects solar power, air management and intelligent controls with homes that use fewer resources. We visit affordable net-zero housing and The Arc House to see how those pieces fit together in everyday life.
green-builder-jan-feb-2018: After a punishing hurricane season, building the same old way doesn't make much sense. We examine where homes fail, products that resist wind and flooding, and projects built to weather trouble. Plus, The Flex House pairs an airtight envelope with lower energy demand and renewable power.
green-builder-jan-feb-2019: Great green building starts with people willing to rethink the usual approach. Meet sustainability educator Nathan Good, explore promising innovations and city programs, and tour our Green Home award winners. Small homes, historic renovations, urban infill and geothermal communities offer plenty of ideas worth borrowing.
green-builder-jan-feb-2020: What does better building look like on the ground? Our sustainability awards recognize Peter Pfeiffer, forward-looking cities and inventive products. Then we tour homes that tackle energy use, ventilation and resilience, from a carefully detailed farmhouse to compact retreats and efficient multifamily living.
green-builder-jan-feb-2021: A smaller footprint doesn't have to mean settling for less. Our sustainability awards celebrate Gene Myers, innovative products and cities moving things forward. Green Home winners bring the ideas home through thoughtful renovations, compact communities, off-grid living and designs that put energy performance to work.
green-builder-jan-feb-2022: There's more than one route to a better home. Our annual awards explore historic renovations, efficient duplexes, net-zero projects and hurricane-conscious building in Puerto Rico. We also recognize Tim O'Brien and communities pushing sustainability forward, with an Austin retrofit offering another practical place to start.
green-builder-jan-feb-2023: Good design earns its keep in everyday life. This issue celebrates Maria Kingery, forward-looking communities and Green Home winners tackling drought, energy use and smaller footprints. We also check in on Mariposa Meadows and Sonders, where air quality and homes that adapt with their owners matter.
green-builder-jan-feb-2024: Resilience belongs in the conversation from the first sketch. Our sustainability awards honor Jon Creyts and cities making progress, then visit homes built for heat, drought, floods and lower energy bills. From compact and prefab designs to net-zero communities, these projects offer useful lessons for the next build.
green-builder-jan-feb-2025: Twenty years in, there's plenty to celebrate—and plenty left to do. Meet our sustainability honorees and Green Home award winners, from historic renovations to storm-ready communities and small-footprint living. We also revisit two decades of Green Builder and explore an Austin home designed for aging in place.
green-builder-jan-feb-2026: Better housing takes more than one good idea. Our sustainability awards recognize Allan Merrill and cities making progress, while this year's Green Home winners explore affordability, prefab construction, renovations and net-zero living. Take a look at the projects turning ambitious goals into places people can call home.
green-builder-jul-aug-2016: Climate change is a big challenge, but businesses and homeowners still have choices. Our Eco-Leaders issue looks at companies changing how they work and ideas for living with a lighter footprint. The focus is on turning environmental concern into decisions that can move things in a better direction.
green-builder-jul-aug-2017: Who's putting sustainability into practice? Meet this year's Eco-Leaders, from major corporations to smaller firms with useful ideas. We also explore healthy homes, attracting investment to efficient projects, and The Flex House, where compact design makes a strong case for living comfortably with less.
green-builder-jul-aug-2018: Hard choices are part of making real progress. Our Eco-Leaders and nine change-making executives show how they're responding to environmental challenges. Meanwhile, The Align Project asks how much space we really need, and Wendell Falls demonstrates that net-zero housing can reach beyond the luxury market.
green-builder-jul-aug-2019: Sustainability needs more than a good slogan. Our Eco-Leaders feature looks at companies addressing climate risk and changing how they operate. We also introduce VISION House Seattle Cascades and visit an updated multifamily project, asking how stronger performance and affordability can fit into the same plan.
green-builder-jul-aug-2020: The pandemic is changing how people use their homes, but the need for lower-impact living hasn't gone away. This issue visits Eco-Leaders working toward net zero and explores changes in kitchens, multifamily housing and outdoor spaces. Mariposa Meadows adds another perspective on designing for a changed world.
green-builder-jul-aug-2022: What happens after a product's first useful life? Our Eco-Leaders issue puts the circular economy in focus, examining environmental declarations, ESG and cradle-to-cradle thinking. It's a look at how businesses can use better information and material choices to raise the bar on building performance.
green-builder-jul-aug-2023: Environmental promises need something measurable behind them. This Eco-Leaders issue explores the building industry's growing use of environmental, social and governance metrics as climate pressures increase. Meet the companies moving that work forward and consider what their approach means for a more accountable building industry.
green-builder-jul-aug-2024: Knowing what's in a product—and how it was made—helps builders make better choices. Our Eco-Leaders issue explores transparency and environmental product declarations. We also look at younger buyers' expectations, stronger building envelopes, Transcend's innovations and the connection between nature and the VISION House Austin design.
green-builder-jul-aug-2025: The rules and the climate keep changing. Our Eco-Leaders issue looks at how companies respond while keeping long-term performance in view. We explore the value of efficient, resilient homes and preview Insight Homes' Peterman II, where building science helps turn those goals into something practical.
green-builder-mar-apr-2016: The yard can do more than hold a lawn. Our landscaping issue explores removing turf, managing stormwater naturally and growing food closer to home. It's a fresh look at outdoor spaces that asks how builders and homeowners can make the land around a house work a little harder.
green-builder-mar-apr-2017: From a Montana ranch to a Passive House and a resilient coastal home, our Green Home award winners take different paths to better living. This issue tours projects that rethink size, energy use and construction, with urban infill and a college demonstration home adding to the mix.
green-builder-mar-apr-2018: An off-grid mountain retreat, a revived Victorian and homes designed for several generations show how varied green building can be. Our award winners combine energy performance with real-life needs. Plus, The Flex House returns with connected technology aimed at saving water, energy and other resources.
green-builder-mar-apr-2019: Choosing products can feel like sorting through a mountain of promises. Our Hot 50 and Readers' Choice coverage help focus the search on performance and useful innovation. The Align Project also steps back to ask how the ways we live and buy shape the homes we need.
green-builder-mar-apr-2020: Which products are moving green building forward? Our Hot 50, Brand Index and Readers' Choice coverage examine the options, from performance and durability to manufacturing practices. Use this issue to compare ideas, question assumptions and find products that deserve a closer look on your next project.
green-builder-mar-apr-2021: Better products are only useful when they solve the right problem. This issue brings together our Hot 50 and Brand Index with a look at product choices for ReVISION House. It's a practical starting point for sorting through the options and connecting them to a home's performance goals.
green-builder-mar-apr-2022: Decarbonizing a home means thinking beyond a single appliance. Our product picks, Decarb Dozen and Brand Index explore the tools, while coverage of electrification considers the load on the grid. We also head outside for ideas on cooking, growing and making outdoor spaces more useful.
green-builder-mar-apr-2023: Looking for a better way to specify your next project? Our annual product issue gathers sustainable options and the Brand Index to help narrow the field. It's a chance to look past familiar habits, compare what matters and find building products that support better-performing homes.
green-builder-mar-apr-2024: A good product choice can pay off long after installation. Our annual products issue explores energy, water and other performance priorities alongside the Brand Index. We also check in with Transcend in Colorado, where travel and housing ideas meet questions about how to live with a lighter footprint.
green-builder-mar-apr-2025: There's no shortage of products competing for a place in a home. Our annual selections and Brand Index help sort through them. We also visit the VISION House projects in Las Vegas and Austin, where upgrades and climate-conscious interiors put performance decisions into a real-world setting.
green-builder-mar-apr-2026: From cleaner indoor air to fire safety, the right products can make a real difference. Our annual sustainable product selections and Brand Index help guide the choices. We also visit Hickory Grove, where partnerships and a focus on workforce housing are part of the affordability story.
green-builder-may-jun-2016: The machines we drive and work with are changing. This issue explores biodiesel work trucks, hybrid excavators and electric cars, looking at cleaner ways to get the job done. It's a reminder that a building project's footprint includes the equipment and travel that make it possible.
green-builder-may-jun-2017: Efficient living isn't just a single-family story. We visit green rental communities, a large Passive House building and a project treating water onsite. The Flex House offers a smaller-scale alternative, while energy-saving products and a closer look at kitchen trends round out the ideas.
green-builder-may-jun-2018: Sometimes the best way forward is to compare notes. This issue looks at how industry associations help builders learn, certify and improve their work. We also introduce The Align Project's compact, modular approach and examine the obstacles keeping many millennials from the homes they'd like to own.
green-builder-may-jun-2019: Smart technology has a useful job to do: helping people stay comfortable and independent as they age. This issue explores assisted living technology, with attention to staying at home longer, using less energy and maintaining a sense of connection. The goal is a better life, not another gadget.
green-builder-may-jun-2020: Building through a pandemic brings questions nobody planned for. This issue hears from industry professionals and manufacturers, then explores bathrooms, air filtration and products designed to ease some of the pressure. It's a look at how housing can respond as health concerns reshape everyday life.
green-builder-may-jun-2022: Fire, floods and heat are testing the places we live. We explore responses ranging from resilient construction to Earthships, along with water concerns and lessons from demanding climates. Sonders, an Austin-area market perspective and a Scottsdale retrofit bring the discussion back to choices builders can make.
green-builder-may-jun-2023: Empty buildings could be part of the answer to the housing shortage. This issue explores conversions, downtown renewal, electrification and bringing nature back into communities. We also look at younger buyers, VISION House Sussex and a barn retrofit that connects a home with a working microfarm.
green-builder-may-jun-2024: Useful change can start with a battery, cleaner air or a better-built home. Meet innovators working on energy and environmental challenges, visit Rheem's home laboratory, and explore Beazer's zero-energy-ready approach in Las Vegas. Younger buyers' expectations help explain why these changes matter to the housing market.
green-builder-may-jun-2025: Resilience doesn't have to begin with a huge budget. This issue explores smaller plans, stronger roofs and attics, thoughtful landscaping and practical technology. We look at how those choices work together—and how alternative construction approaches can help make a more durable, comfortable home attainable.
green-builder-may-jun-2026: What if a home's value included what it costs to live there? This issue introduces Value Per Square Foot, connecting energy, water, resilience, health and community. We also explore living with the elements and VISION House SHAWOOD, asking how better design can deliver value beyond square footage.
green-builder-nov-dec-2016: Energy codes can be confusing, but the details shape the homes we build. This issue explores proposed changes, tradeoffs and enforcement, then visits projects going beyond minimum requirements. A sustainable ranch renovation and The Arc House show different ways to put performance and resilience into practice.
green-builder-nov-dec-2017: There's room to build a better future, but it takes choices now. We explore green roofs and walls, lean urbanism, environmental product declarations and changing energy systems. A closer look at plastics asks whether a growing waste problem can become useful, long-lasting building material.
green-builder-nov-dec-2018: Thinking small can bring some surprisingly big questions. Our Tiny House Tactical Guide covers zoning, financing, building science, water heating and the space people actually need. The Align Project adds a look at intuitive technology, with practical considerations for making compact living work beyond the floor plan.
green-builder-nov-dec-2019: What will shape housing in 2020 and beyond? We examine labor, land and material costs alongside indoor air, connected living and water availability. Project visits add perspective, including a home targeting zero energy, water and sewer use and VISION House Seattle Cascades' approach to performance.
green-builder-nov-dec-2020: Home has taken on a lot of new jobs. Our look ahead to 2021 explores pandemic-driven housing changes, home offices, health and millennial priorities. We also preview Green Home contenders and examine disaster-resistant construction, asking how homes can meet today's needs while preparing for tomorrow's disruptions.
green-builder-nov-dec-2021: The housing market is shifting, and so are buyers' priorities. Our look ahead to 2022 explores decarbonization, material alternatives and changing sales conditions. Electric pickups, an Austin pool project and an aluminum house designed for longevity add practical examples of how the choices are evolving.
green-builder-nov-dec-2022: Housing's next chapter brings climate pressures, supply challenges and new policy opportunities. Our outlook for 2023 explores electrification and ESG alongside labor and materials. We also visit Sonders and Mariposa Meadows, examine Florida insurance concerns and look at Transcend's approach to prefab living.
green-builder-nov-dec-2023: Housing headlines can make the market sound like it's heading in every direction at once. Our annual look at the data sorts through those mixed signals, examining where sales and the broader market may be going. It's a chance to step back from the noise and consider the evidence.
green-builder-nov-dec-2024: Where does sustainable building go next? Our 2025 outlook weighs the economy, election impacts and what builders and buyers are saying. Visits to Las Vegas and Austin bring those questions home, while a narrow Passive House shows how an unusual site can inspire a thoughtful solution.
green-builder-nov-dec-2025: Housing faces policy shifts and an anxious buyer, but demand for better homes persists. Our 2026 outlook explores climate standards, ownership costs and the economics of performance. Hickory Grove's workforce housing, a Passive House preview and a wooden high-rise offer different ideas for the road ahead.
green-builder-q3-2026: A home's real value shows up long after closing day. Our Eco-Leaders issue explores affordability, resilience and the costs of ownership, from insurance to energy. VISION House Asheville and SHAWOOD bring those ideas into focus with designs that put durability, comfort and long-term value to work.
green-builder-sep-oct-2017: Net zero is moving beyond the showcase home. Our building science roundup visits projects using airtight construction, insulation and careful planning to make efficiency more affordable. The Flex House adds water-saving ideas, while a community case study considers how environmental protection and everyday amenities can fit together.
green-builder-sep-oct-2018: A home needs to perform when conditions get tough. This building science issue visits efficient projects, including wildfire-conscious design and well-sealed multifamily housing. The Align Project examines the true cost of ownership, and a look at utilities explores changing energy systems and services.
green-builder-sep-oct-2019: Great performance comes from details working together. Our DOE housing roundup visits net-zero and affordable projects with lessons in planning and product selection. We also explore construction drones, moisture management and VISION House Seattle Cascades, where the full cost of a home matters more than its first price.
green-builder-sep-oct-2020: Electrification and better building science offer practical ways to improve a home. This issue explores retrofit choices and DOE award-winning projects, including resilient and Passive House approaches. A Scottsdale project starts with investigation before demolition, while material shortages prompt a closer look at alternatives.
green-builder-sep-oct-2021: Better performance starts with the basics done well. Our DOE housing roundup explores insulation, air sealing, efficient systems and projects using ICFs and SIPs. Indoor air quality and an Austin HVAC project connect those technical choices to the comfort and health people want from their homes.
green-builder-sep-oct-2022: Smaller, stronger and more efficient homes can offer a lot to learn from. Our DOE awards coverage explores resilient construction, Passive House ideas and heat pumps. We also check in on Mariposa Meadows and Transcend communities, with shifting millennial preferences adding context to the housing conversation.
green-builder-sep-oct-2023: Good building science can serve first-time buyers as well as custom homes. Our DOE roundup explores affordable projects, attached housing, efficient envelopes and renewable energy choices. Younger buyers' expectations and VISION House Sussex add perspective on how better-performing homes fit into a changing market.
green-builder-sep-oct-2024: Efficient homes come in more than one shape. Our DOE winners include multifamily projects, Passive House approaches and affordable housing, with indoor air quality and density part of the story. We also explore younger buyers' interest in green credentials and the VISION House projects in Las Vegas and Austin.
green-builder-sep-oct-2025: Better homes need to work for real budgets and real lives. Our DOE winners explore affordable communities, resilient townhomes and efficient construction. We also look at practical uses of AI, Hickory Grove's duplex approach and Transcend's manufactured housing, finding useful ideas across very different kinds of projects.
green-builder-spring-2018: The product aisle is crowded. Our Hot 50 selections help narrow it down across energy, water, indoor air, building envelopes and connected technology. Readers' Choice results add another perspective on trusted brands and trends, giving builders a starting point for asking better questions about the next specification.
green-builder-q4-2026: Housing’s in a tough spot, but there’s plenty worth building on. In this issue, we look at what buyers really want in 2027, how to ease the monthly payment squeeze, and how to build homes that can take a hit. Plus, our VISION House projects in Asheville and Deerlake Ranch show how better design can make homes healthier, more comfortable, and ready for whatever comes next.
